context: Step 1: characterization test capturing current outputs of all three implementations over shared fixture data (including edge cases: zero/negative times filtered by analytics.py:260-269 run_type=='measurement' and ms>0, odd/even counts, single element). Step 2: extend core with any missing functions, choosing one percentile definition; record the rationale in the module docstring. Step 3: migrate mcp/tools/analytics.py and cli/commands/aggregate.py onto core; delete local copies. Step 4: cross-surface equivalence test (same fixture -> identical numbers via CLI aggregate path and MCP analytics path). If chosen-method outputs differ from a surface's previous outputs, list the delta explicitly in the PR description.
description: Three implementations of the same statistics exist: benchbox/core/results/metrics.py (canonical), benchbox/mcp/tools/analytics.py:932-971 (_calculate_metric geometric mean via logs, _percentile linear interpolation, _std_dev sample variance), and benchbox/cli/commands/aggregate.py:154-174 (_compute_query_statistics geomean/p50/p95/p99). For a benchmarking product this is a credibility defect: the same result files can yield different numbers per surface. Consolidate on one core module (extend core/results/metrics.py or a sibling statistics module) and migrate both consumers. Percentile interpolation methods may genuinely differ between the three copies -- characterize first, pick one method deliberately, and document the choice.

anti_patterns.dont: leave a params-compatible copy of _percentile in mcp or cli 'for fallback'
anti_patterns.instead: delete the local copies in the same PR
anti_patterns.why: the whole point is one implementation; fallbacks resurrect drift

anti_patterns.dont: silently change reported numbers during migration
anti_patterns.instead: characterize first; any numeric delta is listed explicitly in the PR
anti_patterns.why: published/archived results are compared against new runs; unexplained metric shifts destroy trust

preserves.behavior: MCP analytics measurement-row filter semantics (run_type=='measurement', ms>0) keep their current behavior.
TPCMetricsCalculator's existing public API is extended, not broken.
aggregate CSV column contract: existing output columns keep names and order.
